official_admissions.title: Business cycle and herding behavior in stock returns: theory and evidence

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed; model equations/results inspected as needed to calibrate claims.

summary_architecture: close with practical significance and explicit robustness needs
rhetoric.evidence_order: Observed recession/boom pattern precedes the proposed uncertainty channel; the channel is tested after the directional relationship is established.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Magnitude and fit statistics follow the directional result; numbers support the argument rather than lead it.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Useful mixed example. The paper initially treats uncertainty as a conjectured/intermediary channel, but later uses stronger language ('explains through' / 'confirm') than the observational chain alone securely identifies. Preserve this tension as an anti-pattern.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Mechanism is first introduced with conjectural language; later prose becomes more categorical.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Boom versus recession is integral to the thesis; the paper does not present an unconditional average as the whole result.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S. stock market; annual business-cycle framing; proxy-based herding and uncertainty measures.
rhetoric.limitations: Conclusion explicitly says the empirical setting was designed to confirm a theoretical toy model and calls for more controls and robustness of the transmission channel.
rhetoric.implications: Policy/investor implications follow the empirical regime result, but should not inherit stronger causal certainty than the design supports.
anti_patterns: Do not let sequential associations automatically become a fully identified causal transmission channel.
Do not let a theoretical model upgrade empirical identification by itself.

atomic_observations.observation: When the substantive effect changes with the business-cycle regime, the regime belongs in the main finding rather than a late caveat.
A proposed channel should be linguistically weaker than the directly observed relationship unless the design identifies the channel.
A robustness need is most useful when attached to the exact channel or empirical setting it constrains.
The relationship is easier to interpret when the directional result comes before the mechanism and before detailed statistics.

official_admissions.title: Changepoint detection in the cross-section of stock returns

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed; technical model specifications and results inspected where needed.

summary_architecture: separate mean, variance, and distributional changes
test how much conventional factor models absorb
translate residual pattern into model-validation implications
rhetoric.evidence_order: Existence/robustness first; type and horizon of instability second; explanatory-model performance third; implications last.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The authors repeatedly distinguish counts/statistical evidence from economic interpretation. Method-dependent counts are contextualized rather than treated as interchangeable; persistent monthly volatility regimes receive more economic weight than transient daily breaks.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Mechanistic explanations for why factor performance changes are labeled as possible explanations or conjectures, not established causes.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Confidence is strong about the existence of instability and weaker about why it exists.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Frequency/horizon is a first-order boundary: daily breaks can be transient/noisy while monthly breaks are more consistent with persistent regimes.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Partial explanation is expressed as mitigation without elimination rather than as success/failure binary.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S. stock-return cross-section; conclusions depend on horizon, method family, and model specification.
rhetoric.limitations: Residual instability is explicitly retained rather than hidden after factor adjustment; different detection thresholds are discussed as part of interpretation.
rhetoric.implications: A useful model should reduce residual instability, not merely improve conventional fit.
anti_patterns: Do not equate statistical detection at a high-frequency horizon with economically persistent regime change.
Do not call a model explanatory success when it improves fit but leaves the core instability largely intact.

atomic_observations.observation: Statistical strength and economic persistence are separate judgments.
'Mitigates but does not eliminate' is appropriate when a model explains only part of a pattern.
If aggregation changes the substantive interpretation, the time horizon belongs in the conclusion.
Agreement across method families strengthens confidence that a phenomenon exists without identifying its mechanism.

official_admissions.title: Google search volume index and investor attention in stock market: a systematic review

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including search/quality process, classification, findings, limits, and conclusion.

rhetoric.evidence_order: Consistent relationships (volatility/volume) are separated from the mixed return literature; classification variables explain why a universal return thesis is inappropriate.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Counts/percentages characterize corpus composition and consistency; substantive conclusions are expressed as cross-study patterns rather than a parade of metrics.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The review mainly summarizes association/prediction and does not need causal verbs to make its strongest points.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Conditional language is used when relationships vary by keyword construction, geography, and frequency.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Returns are treated as mixed/conditional while volatility and trading volume are comparatively consistent.
rhetoric.null_result_language: The review preserves studies with no universal relationship instead of forcing them into positive/negative bins.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Geography, query construction, data frequency, and uneven regional representation materially bound generalization.
rhetoric.limitations: Regional representation is explicitly uneven. The paper also contains a corpus-count inconsistency: it repeatedly describes 56 articles while parts of the selection narrative have been reported differently in the inherited notes; preserve the published wording rather than silently harmonizing it.
rhetoric.implications: Future research requests are tied to concrete unresolved design choices such as keyword validity, longitudinal comparison, and practical profitability after costs.
anti_patterns: Do not flatten a literature when one outcome is consistent and another is heterogeneous.
Do not hide scope imbalance behind a global-sounding synthesis.

atomic_observations.observation: A synthesis can state a strong conclusion for one outcome and a conditional conclusion for another in the same evidence base.
Named coverage gaps are stronger than generic 'more research is needed' caveats.
Corpus percentages should establish evidence coverage, not dominate the prose.
Use 'depends on' when design choices materially change the observed relationship.

official_admissions.title: Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns: new theory and evidence
official_admissions.journal: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed; theory derivations and robustness tests inspected where needed.

summary_architecture: decompose sentiment into long- and short-run components
close by matching empirical pattern back to theory
rhetoric.evidence_order: Theory establishes expected signs; empirical results follow; alternative rational explanations are then tested before the conclusion returns to the main interpretation.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Magnitude is used mainly to compare exposure across sentiment-prone versus sentiment-immune portfolios and across characteristics.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The paper carefully distinguishes the theoretical mechanism from empirical association and explicitly tests whether systematic risk could produce the same cross-sectional pattern. 'Suggests' is used after those alternative-explanation tests rather than assuming the behavioral story.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Potential rational explanations are introduced explicitly before being tested; plausible explanations are not stated as facts.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Effects vary with size, age, volatility, distress/growth characteristics, and exposure to sentiment; aggregate market regressions can be weak while cross-sectional effects remain strong.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Little evidence at the aggregate market level is retained and used to clarify why the cross-sectional result is the relevant object.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: The result is about differential exposure across stocks and should not be rewritten as an unconditional statement about aggregate market returns.
rhetoric.limitations: Competing systematic-risk explanations are treated as threats to interpretation and explicitly tested rather than relegated to generic caveats.
rhetoric.implications: The main implication is structural: the same market-wide sentiment can affect assets differently depending on sentiment exposure and arbitrage constraints.
sentence_relations: behavioral interpretation -> competing risk explanation -> robustness
anti_patterns: Do not convert a cross-sectional result into an aggregate-market claim.
Do not present the preferred mechanism before confronting an observationally plausible alternative.

atomic_observations.observation: Cross-sectional evidence can be strong even when aggregate-market evidence is weak; the summary must preserve that level of analysis.
A preferred mechanism becomes more credible when the prose explicitly states and tests a competing explanation.
Material characteristic-level differences belong in the synthesis when they determine exposure to the main relationship.
Theoretical prediction language and empirical finding language should remain distinct.

official_admissions.title: An empirical examination of investor sentiment and stock market volatility: evidence from India

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including sentiment construction, GARCH/Granger design, interpretation, and conclusion.

summary_architecture: construct composite index from market proxies including advance-decline breadth
test temporal precedence with Granger framework
rhetoric.evidence_order: Measurement construction precedes volatility modeling; temporal-prediction result precedes a behavioral interpretation.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Model diagnostics justify the volatility specification before substantive interpretation; the prose is more useful when it reports direction/persistence than when it extrapolates to broad market-efficiency claims.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Important anti-pattern. Granger causality establishes predictive temporal information, not structural causation. The paper sometimes moves from 'leads' to 'significantly causes' and broad efficiency conclusions. The corpus should learn the earlier calibrated phrasing, not the later overreach.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Mechanism paragraphs contain useful 'may'/'can be explained' qualifiers, but the conclusion becomes less disciplined.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Positive and negative sentiment effects are asymmetric; volatility persistence and crisis-era behavior are treated separately.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Reverse temporal relationship is reported as not found rather than omitted.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Indian/Nifty setting; monthly data; composite sentiment proxy; Granger framework.
rhetoric.limitations: Future-work request focuses on higher-frequency and more comprehensive sentiment measurement; causal identification remains a stronger implicit limitation than the article acknowledges.
rhetoric.implications: Investor/policy recommendations should be weakened relative to the paper's strongest prose because the design is predictive/associational rather than structural-causal.
anti_patterns: Do not translate Granger causality into structural 'X causes Y' language.
Do not infer broad market inefficiency from one proxy/model result without preserving design and market boundaries.
Do not let policy recommendations exceed the certainty of the empirical design.

atomic_observations.observation: When a constructed index includes a breadth measure, say what the index captures rather than treating the proxy as the latent concept itself.
'Leads' or 'predicts' is safer than structural causal wording for Granger results.
Positive/negative asymmetry should be stated as such rather than averaged into a single sentiment effect.
A strong-looking econometric label can invite prose that outruns what the design identifies; the summary must independently police that boundary.

official_admissions.title: Herding behavior in Ramadan and financial crises: the case of the Pakistani stock market

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including CSSD/CSAD design, market-state tests, results, and conclusion.

summary_architecture: split by market direction, volume, volatility, calendar, and crisis
rhetoric.evidence_order: Broad no-herding result comes before the narrower conditions where herding is detected; the exceptions therefore refine rather than replace the baseline.

overstrong_mechanism_to_avoid: due to higher uncertainty and information asymmetry

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Signs/significance of dispersion coefficients are translated into presence/absence decisions; the main prose value is the state-dependent contrast.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The empirical design identifies state-dependent herding patterns, not the cause of those patterns. The conclusion's attribution of crisis herding to uncertainty/information asymmetry should be retained as an anti-pattern unless separately identified.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Nulls are often stated directly; explanatory mechanisms are less carefully qualified.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Low-volume days and the 2007–08 crisis differ from full-sample, up/down, high/low-volatility, and Ramadan states.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Particularly useful: repeated 'no evidence' statements are preserved before conditional exceptions.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Pakistani/Karachi Stock Exchange; specific sample period; CSSD/CSAD definitions capture particular forms of market-wide herding.
rhetoric.limitations: Method choice bounds what 'no herding' means; absence under CSSD/CSAD is not evidence that every form of coordinated behavior is absent.
rhetoric.implications: The useful implication is conditional—crowding can emerge under particular volume/crisis states—not a universal claim of irrationality.
anti_patterns: Do not rewrite 'no evidence of herding under this test' as evidence that herding does not exist in any form.
Do not attach an untested mechanism to a conditional empirical result as if it were identified.
Do not infer broad market inefficiency solely from state-specific herding.

atomic_observations.observation: 'No evidence under this test/condition' is more precise than 'herding does not exist.'
A mostly null result with narrow regime exceptions should be summarized as conditional evidence, not as a binary positive finding.
The measurement definition determines what kind of crowding a null can actually reject.
State dependence does not by itself identify why the state changes behavior.

official_admissions.title: Trading behavior-stock market volatility nexus among institutional and individual investors

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including theory, hypotheses, model selection, empirical results, strategy/performance analysis, conclusion, and notes.

summary_architecture: define investor groups and competing literature
separate buy/sell positions and pre/post-pandemic regimes
select econometric specification before interpreting coefficients
compare behavioral asymmetry and strategy performance
rhetoric.evidence_order: Model specification precedes interpretation; group/position/regime differences are reported before behavioral explanation.

caution: herd behavior requires care when inferred from momentum/feedback trading rather than directly identified

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Coefficients matter through comparison across investor type, position, and regime; isolated numbers are not rhetorically useful.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Dynamic spillover/interdependence is the best-supported language. The model does not by itself identify a clean structural causal mechanism.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Strongest when relationships are described as varying by group, position, and period; weaker where behavioral labels are inferred from trading patterns.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Investor type, buy/sell position, and pre-pandemic/pandemic periods materially alter magnitude and direction.
rhetoric.null_result_language: One-way and absent relationships are kept separate from the bidirectional findings rather than pooled.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Istanbul/Turkish market; specific investor classifications; model-dependent spillover estimates; COVID regime split.
rhetoric.limitations: Some survey/strategy detail is omitted for paper-length reasons; econometric sophistication does not itself establish structural causality.
rhetoric.implications: Market behavior can shift with participant composition and trading position, but that compositional explanation must remain calibrated to evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not use model sophistication as a license for stronger causal prose.
Do not collapse institutional and retail participants when their responses differ.
Do not infer herding solely from momentum-like behavior.

atomic_observations.observation: When participant groups respond differently, name the group rather than summarize a market-wide average.
Buy/sell asymmetry should survive compression when it changes the conclusion.
A change in participant mix can help explain regime differences, but remains interpretation unless independently identified.
'Spillover' or 'bidirectional relationship' is often more faithful than structural causal wording for multivariate volatility models.

official_admissions.title: Effects of investor sentiment on stock volatility: new evidences from multi-source data in China’s green stock markets

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including sample/proxy construction, baseline models, board subsamples, mediation analysis, COVID split, robustness, and conclusion.

rhetoric.evidence_order: Baseline association precedes component, subgroup, mediation, and regime analysis.

caution: 'affects through' is stronger than warranted when observational mediation is treated as an identified causal path

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Exact coefficients and mediation percentages are useful after the directional comparison is established; ratios show regime change without replacing the thesis.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Fixed-effects/stepwise mediation plus bootstrap supports a mediation pattern, not by itself a structurally identified causal channel.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Some explanations are qualified with 'may'; channel language later becomes more categorical than the design warrants.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Effects vary by volatility component, board, sentiment source, and pre/post-COVID period.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Insignificant subgroup effects are reported and materially narrow the aggregate thesis.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: 106 Chinese green stocks; 2019–2020 window; specific sentiment/VPIN constructions; pandemic split.
rhetoric.limitations: Short sample and specialized green-stock setting constrain generalization; identification limits are more important than the paper's explicit limitations language suggests.
rhetoric.implications: Regulatory implications should remain conditional because the strongest evidence is associational/mediation-pattern evidence rather than a policy experiment.
anti_patterns: Do not promote statistical mediation to an identified causal mechanism without design support.
Do not generalize a specialized market/sample to all equities.
Do not bury an insignificant subgroup that narrows the thesis.

atomic_observations.observation: If an outcome decomposes into components with different sensitivities, preserve the component that drives the result.
An aggregate positive relationship can coexist with an insignificant subgroup effect; both should be stated.
Statistical mediation is best summarized as evidence consistent with a channel unless the channel is causally identified.
Use direct before/after magnitude comparison when a regime split materially changes sensitivity.

official_admissions.title: Revisiting the trading activity of high-frequency trading firms around ultra-fast flash events

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: All substantive prose sections reviewed, including event definitions, methodology, event/regression/logit analyses, robustness windows, conclusion, and data boundaries.

summary_architecture: separate event-study, controlled-regression, and trigger-test evidence
make method sensitivity part of the conclusion
rhetoric.evidence_order: Measurement problem precedes the result because the measurement choice changes the answer; event behavior is kept distinct from trigger evidence.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Threshold and event-window robustness are used to test whether the substantive conclusion survives alternative definitions.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Excellent distinction between participating in/reinforcing a crash and triggering it; 'no evidence they trigger' is not converted to proof of impossibility.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Policy language is cautionary because results are methodology- and data-dependent.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Normal periods and ultra-fast stress events produce different liquidity behavior.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Strong example of preserving a precise null about triggering while reporting positive evidence about behavior during an event.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: U.S./Nasdaq-centered data; HFT group-level rather than firm-level identification; some integrated firms/routed orders absent; event-definition dependent.
rhetoric.limitations: Geography, aggregation level, and missing trader classifications are named explicitly.
rhetoric.implications: Methodology sensitivity is itself actionable: stability claims should not be made without testing alternative event definitions.
anti_patterns: Do not confuse behavior during an event with causing the event.
Do not hide method sensitivity when it changes the conclusion.
Do not turn 'no evidence of triggering' into proof of impossibility.

atomic_observations.observation: Separate 'participates in/reinforces an event' from 'triggers the event' when tests identify different temporal relationships.
If the substantive result changes with event definition, methodology sensitivity belongs in the main conclusion.
Cautionary policy language is appropriate when identification choices materially affect the answer.
Data coverage at group versus firm level should constrain the grammatical subject of the conclusion.

official_admissions.title: Stock Market Volatility and Return Analysis: A Systematic Literature Review

jif.verification: MDPI Entropy journal imprint / journal metrics

full_text.source: MDPI open-access full article; corroborated by PubMed Central record
full_text.review_scope: Substantive prose reviewed from abstract/introduction through systematic search methodology, study synthesis, model comparisons, and conclusion. Tables/search strings were inspected where needed to understand the review design and evidence ordering.

summary_architecture: motivate volatility as a market problem
rhetoric.evidence_order: The review defines the question and search process before comparing models. Its strongest passages move from cross-study pattern to model tradeoff rather than listing individual papers.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Counts describe review coverage and screening attrition. Model comparisons are primarily qualitative; the useful rhetorical lesson is that corpus size establishes scope but does not itself establish a substantive conclusion.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The review does not need causal language for its central contribution. It is strongest when describing comparative model performance and weakest where generalized recommendations are broader than the heterogeneous underlying studies.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Model performance is often phrased conditionally; no single GARCH-family model is treated as universally best.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Market type, input structure, model class, and forecasting context affect which modeling choice is most appropriate.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Uses non-binary comparative language such as performance being 'not always satisfactory' rather than forcing a universal winner.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Review window 2008–2019; English-language literature; Scopus/Web of Science search; emphasis on GARCH-family stock-return/volatility studies.
rhetoric.limitations: The review's narrow model-family/search criteria bound what can be generalized to all volatility research. Its prose also demonstrates why descriptive literature counts should not substitute for analytical synthesis.
rhetoric.implications: Model choice should preserve the tradeoff between parsimony, flexibility, and the market/data setting rather than follow one universal hierarchy.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a review count as substantive evidence by itself.
Do not promote a context-dependent model comparison into a universal ranking.
Do not hide narrow search criteria when they define the evidence universe.

atomic_observations.observation: A review should establish how its evidence universe was constructed before making cross-study claims.
When alternatives differ on multiple dimensions, comparative language can preserve the tradeoff instead of declaring a single winner.
Cross-study pattern should precede individual methodological detail when the purpose is synthesis.
Search window, databases, language, and model-family restrictions materially limit what a review conclusion can claim.

official_admissions.title: Cross-sectional anomalies and conditional asset pricing models based on investor sentiment: evidence from the Chinese stock market

jif.verification: Springer Nature Financial Innovation journal metrics

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: Substantive prose reviewed across framing, methodology, data construction, equal/value-weight anomaly tests, conditional-model results, pandemic subsample analysis, limitations, and conclusion.

rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper establishes which anomalies survive before asking whether conditioning information explains them. Aggregate model improvement is then separated from anomaly-specific failures.

regime: when the pandemic period is excluded

rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Equal-weight versus value-weight comparisons and anomaly significance are interpreted before detailed coefficients. The weighting choice itself becomes economically meaningful because some anomalies disappear under capitalization weighting.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The evidence supports explanatory/predictive improvement in conditional asset-pricing models, not a claim that sentiment structurally causes every anomaly.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: The conclusion retains unexplained anomalies and does not claim complete model closure.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Weighting scheme, anomaly type, model family, and pandemic inclusion all change the strength of the conclusion.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Unexplained turnover and turnover-volatility anomalies are retained as model failures rather than hidden behind overall improvement.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Chinese A-shares; 2007–2022; selected 30 previously supported anomalies; specific sentiment proxy and conditional CAPM/FF3 framework.
rhetoric.limitations: The authors explicitly state the model does not encompass all anomalies and lacks an effective high-frequency anomaly/instrument strategy for pandemic conditions.
rhetoric.implications: A model can improve materially while remaining incomplete; the summary should preserve both the gain and the residual failure.
anti_patterns: Do not turn better explanatory power into complete explanation.
Do not collapse equal-weight and capitalization-weighted evidence if the anomaly changes under weighting.
Do not let an aggregate improvement erase anomaly-specific failures.

atomic_observations.observation: A better model can still leave important outcomes unexplained; both facts belong in the synthesis.
When equal- and value-weight results differ materially, weighting is part of the substantive interpretation rather than a technical footnote.
If a shock period reduces the usefulness of a signal, report the regime dependence rather than averaging the result across the full sample.
Naming which anomalies remain unexplained is more informative than saying the model is imperfect.

official_admissions.title: Online investor disagreement, self-attribution bias, and future stock returns

jif.verification: Springer Nature Financial Innovation journal metrics

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: Substantive prose reviewed across theory/hypotheses, measurement assumptions, fixed-effect regressions, sentiment and return results, COVID robustness checks, mechanism claims, limitations, and conclusion.

summary_architecture: connect disagreement to aggregate sentiment and returns
rhetoric.evidence_order: The paper tests the proposed mechanism in stages rather than jumping directly from disagreement to returns. Measurement limitations are stated before the stronger return interpretation.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: Magnitude is used to demonstrate asymmetric sentiment shifts and short-term return/reversal patterns. The prose is strongest where sign, horizon, and participant type are named before coefficient detail.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: The staged mechanism tests are stronger than a single correlation, but the authors themselves acknowledge measurement imprecision. A safe synthesis should describe the evidence as supporting/consistent with the self-attribution mechanism rather than treating it as fully identified structural causality.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Specific measurement assumptions and generalizability limits are explicit, which appropriately weakens universal claims.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Optimistic and pessimistic investors respond asymmetrically; effects differ after rising versus falling prices; short-term effects later reverse.
rhetoric.null_result_language: Neutral-investor responses can be insignificant even when the optimistic/pessimistic groups show clear asymmetry.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Chinese online-investor forum data; individual-investor-heavy population; monthly bias classification assumptions; conclusions may not extend to institutions.
rhetoric.limitations: The paper explicitly notes polarized-opinion truncation, inability to extract some bias measures daily, sample constraints, and limited generalizability to sophisticated institutional participants.
rhetoric.implications: The grammatical subject matters: evidence about online individual investors should not silently become a statement about all market participants.
anti_patterns: Do not generalize online-retail evidence to all investors.
Do not suppress a later reversal when it changes the economic meaning of a short-term effect.
Do not state a proposed psychological mechanism more strongly than its measurement supports.

atomic_observations.observation: The grammatical subject of a summary must retain the participant population actually observed.
A short-term effect followed by reversal should be summarized as a sequence, not as a single directional return effect.
A mechanism claim should weaken when the underlying behavioral measure relies on coarse temporal classification or indirect proxies.
Opposite reactions among initially optimistic and pessimistic groups are analytically meaningful and should not be averaged away.

official_admissions.title: Volatility spillovers, structural breaks and uncertainty in technology sector markets

jif.verification: Springer Nature Financial Innovation journal metrics

full_text.source: Springer Nature open-access full HTML version of record
full_text.review_scope: Substantive prose reviewed across literature framing, DCC/structural-break methodology, data, time-varying co-movement results, uncertainty tests, portfolio interpretation, limitations, and conclusion.

rhetoric.evidence_order: Baseline dynamic correlations are established before structural-break and uncertainty overlays; the conclusion then synthesizes which relationships are stable and which depend on shock type.
rhetoric.quantitative_presentation: The paper uses changing correlations and portfolio weights to demonstrate that sector relationships are time-varying; the summary value comes from direction and heterogeneity rather than coefficient recitation.
rhetoric.causal_calibration: Structural breaks and uncertainty regressions support changed connectedness, but explanatory stories about why specific sectors behave differently remain interpretation.
rhetoric.uncertainty_and_modality: Shock type is repeatedly named because EPU, VIX, currency volatility, and other uncertainty measures do not produce one uniform response.
rhetoric.heterogeneity_and_regime: Technology subsectors differ from one another, and the same subsector can change its linkage after breaks or under different uncertainty measures.
rhetoric.null_result_language: The paper avoids one universal hedge/diversifier characterization and instead reports where relationships are weak, negative, or unstable.
rhetoric.boundary_conditions: Different series use different sample periods; technology represented by specific subsector indices; VIX is the stock-volatility proxy.
rhetoric.limitations: Authors explicitly identify inconsistent data periods and reliance on VIX as the stock-volatility proxy.
rhetoric.implications: Sector-level Market commentary should preserve subsector and shock-type heterogeneity when those differences determine the result.
anti_patterns: Do not summarize a heterogeneous technology complex as one uniform sector response.
Do not treat every uncertainty proxy as interchangeable.
Do not convert a co-movement shift into a causal explanation for the sector without separate identification.

atomic_observations.observation: When subsectors move differently, a sector-level summary should either name the dominant divergence or avoid a single-sector generalization.
If different uncertainty measures change the relationship in different directions, name the shock type rather than writing 'uncertainty increases/decreases X.'
A relationship that changes after a structural break should be summarized dynamically rather than by its full-sample average.
A conclusion about market volatility is bounded by the volatility proxy used; the proxy should matter when alternative measures could change interpretation.

observations_so_far.observation: Across the admitted set, the cleanest prose states the empirical relationship at the strength supported by the design, then uses weaker modality for the explanatory mechanism unless that mechanism is independently identified.
Market relationships frequently depend on regime, horizon, characteristic, volume, or measurement definition. Strong synthesis names the condition rather than averaging it away.
'No evidence of X under this test/condition' carries materially different information from 'X does not exist.'
When conventional factors or models reduce but leave a phenomenon intact, 'mitigates but does not eliminate' preserves both the explanatory contribution and the residual problem.
Directional/comparative meaning generally precedes detailed magnitudes; numbers then establish scale, robustness, or heterogeneity rather than functioning as a standalone summary.

Some admitted papers contain useful substantive evidence but rhetorically overstate Granger causality, intermediary channels, or broad market-efficiency implications. Those passages are retained as negative training observations rather than copied as style.

observations_so_far.theme: grammatical subject must match evidence scope
observations_so_far.observation: When evidence is specific to an investor class, volatility component, event window, or data aggregation level, the sentence subject should retain that scope instead of silently becoming 'the market.'
If alternative definitions or identification methods change the finding, that methodological dependence belongs in the conclusion rather than being treated as housekeeping.

Equal-weight and capitalization-weight evidence can support different conclusions; when weighting changes the observed anomaly or breadth signal, the weighting choice is part of the meaning rather than an implementation detail.

Market effects can reverse after an initial horizon. Good compression preserves sequences such as short-run continuation followed by reversal instead of turning the first interval into a timeless directional claim.
Systematic-review language is strongest when the evidence universe and screening method are explicit before cross-study conclusions; review counts establish coverage, not truth.
